text_blocks.snippet: CPR plus Automated External Defibrillation (AED) should ideally be started within 3-5 minutes of collapse to significantly boost survival chances in cases of cardiac arrest. Early intervention with both CPR and AED is crucial for maintaining blood flow and restoring a normal heart rhythm, minimizing the risk of irreversible damage to vital organs like the brain.
Here's why this timeframe is so critical:

list.title: Brain Damage:
list.snippet: Without oxygenated blood, the brain can start to suffer damage within minutes of cardiac arrest.

list.title: Increased Survival:
list.snippet: Studies show that the likelihood of survival decreases by about 7-10% for every minute that passes without CPR and defibrillation.
